subject: CLOSE statement
notes: DERIVED FIRST: a CLOSE naming more than one file-name must be rejected when it appears in imperative-statement-1 (region A) of a Format-3 exception-checking PERFORM -- and ONLY there, since the rule names imperative-statement-1 specifically and not the WHEN/FINALLY bodies. READ: EcBinder.CheckCrossStatementBans builds `regionA = p.statementBlock()` (imperative-statement-1) separately from `whenBodies`/`finallyBody`, and emits `foreach (var cl in regionA.SelectMany(Descendants<Core.CloseStatementContext>).Where(s => s.closeFilePhrase().Length > 1)) ctx.Edition.Error("COBOL1612", "a multi-file CLOSE shall not appear in imperative-statement-1 of an exception-checking PERFORM (ISO 14.9.6.3 SR3)")`. MATCHED on all three axes: the region is regionA only (not regionB, which the neighbouring 1604/1605/1606/1607 checks use for whole-PERFORM bans); the predicate is `closeFilePhrase().Length > 1`, which is exactly 'specifies more than one file-name' and correctly counts file-names rather than closeOptions; and `Descendants<>` reaches a CLOSE nested inside an inner statement of imperative-statement-1, which the rule requires since imperative-statement-1 is a statement list. EDITIONS: 2023 only -- the Format-3 exception-checking PERFORM is new in this edition ('Inline exception processing. The PERFORM statement is enhanced to allow checking for exception conditions inline'), and the construct itself is gated by VersionConformancePass.VisitPerformStatement -> Constructs.PerformExceptionChecking2023, so the rule cannot apply below 2023. TEST EVIDENCE, spec-derived and two-sided: PerformFormat3Tests.MultiFileCloseInImp1_Rejected1612 asserts `PERFORM CLOSE F1 F2 WHEN EC-SIZE ... END-PERFORM` is rejected with COBOL1612, and PerformFormat3Tests.MultiFileCloseInWhenBody_Accepted_NoBan asserts the same CLOSE in a WHEN body is NOT flagged -- the complement that proves the region discrimination, not just the rejection. Row closed. || UPHELD, with one citation correction and two edges I checked that the note did not. CITATION CORRECTED: the 'Inline exception processing' item is Annex E.2 item 19 (specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 43058), NOT E.3 -- E.3 begins at line 43189, after it; the quoted text is verbatim and the 2023-only edition claim it supports is therefore sound, but the note cited it one section off, which is precisely the inherited-citation failure mode. EDGE 1 (the Format-3 discriminator): I checked that the ban cannot be dodged by writing a Format-3 PERFORM with no WHEN phrase. ControlFlowBinder.IsFormat3 (ControlFlowBinder.cs:167-171) routes to EcBindExceptionPerform on ANY of performWhenPhrase / performWhenOther / performWhenCommon / performFinally / a [WITH] LOCATION head, so a `PERFORM ... FINALLY ... END-PERFORM` still reaches CheckCrossStatementBans. EDGE 2 (the walk): I read `Descendants<T>` (EcBinder.ExceptionPerform.cs:320-328) and confirmed it is a full recursive parse-tree walk, so a multi-file CLOSE nested inside an IF or an inline PERFORM within imperative-statement-1 is caught -- the rule's 'specified in imperative-statement-1' is lexical containment, and the grammar (CobolControlFlow.g4:32-34, `PERFORM performInlineHead? statementBlock* performWhenPhrase* ...`) makes `p.statementBlock()` exactly the imp-1 children, which the WHEN-body complement test independently proves. I verified both tests exist and assert what the note says (PerformFormat3Tests.cs:85-86 and :127-133). Row closed.
